key_insight: The paper gives an end-to-end theory showing how diffusion model quality is jointly controlled by finite-sample score learning, network training, and sampling discretization.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical error budget that can guide choices of dataset size, time-step grids, and optimization accuracy when implementing diffusion samplers.
method: Derive a unified generalization and convergence analysis for score-based diffusion models with ResNet-type parameterizations.
Decompose terminal total variation error into truncation, reverse-time discretization, generalization, and optimization-gap terms.
Connect the learned discrete-time score training problem to the ideal continuous-time population objective.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an end-to-end total variation distance estimate for the generated terminal distribution, with explicit decomposition of the generative error into four components.
watch_item: The guarantees are theoretical and depend on idealized assumptions about model class, discretization, and optimization, so direct numerical tightness in large-scale deployments may vary.
paper_title: From Score Learning to Discretized Sampling: An End-to-End Generalization Analysis of Diffusion Models
